newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Savage says 2nd half outlook brighter.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Savage says 2nd half outlook brighter.

text.p: Base metals and coal miner Savage Resources Ltd said on Friday the outlook for the second half had improved significantly following a pick-up in zinc prices.
Savage earlier reported net profit halved to A$5.52 million in the half year to December 31 from A$11.15 million a year earlier.
The result had been foreshadowed at Savage's annual general meeting in November.
Managing director Jim Wall said the fall was due mainly to flat zinc prices and lower germanium and acid sales.
Wall said the company's coal operations in the New South Wales' Hunter Valley continued to perform strongly, although coal prices had been weakening.
However, he noted the LME zinc price had risen to a two year high on January 21.
Zinc is currently trading around 51.5 US cents a pound.
Wall said Savage expected to produce and sell about 53,000 tonnes of zinc metal in the next six months.
"In the current operating environment, each U.S. one cent rise in the LME zinc price adds about A$2 million a year to Savage's pre-tax profit," he said.
Zinc made up about A$90.9 million of Savage's half-year operating revenue of A$125.1 million, producing an operating profit of A$4.3 million.
Coal operations produced an operating profit of A$6.3 million from operating revenue of A$32.3 million.
